issues.body: ReleaseOnlyWorkflowInertnessTests.test_no_rust_ci_workflow_invokes_a_release_only_workflow scans only OrchestrationSafeInertnessTests._RUST_CI_WORKFLOWS. The invariant documented by the change is stronger: no allowlisted workflow may be uses:-invoked by any workflow that runs on pull_request, pull_request_target, or merge_group. The repository has many PR-triggered workflows outside that hand-maintained list, and a new caller there would not fail this test. In that state an allowlisted workflow can change a PR result, yet ci_select will continue suppressing the full selection for edits to it, contradicting the stated inertness proof.
issues.fix_hint: Derive the caller corpus from every workflow under .github/workflows whose parsed top-level on block contains a PR/merge-group trigger, instead of using _RUST_CI_WORKFLOWS. Also account for transitive reusable-workflow calls (or explicitly compute reachability from PR-triggered roots), so a PR workflow calling an intermediate reusable workflow that calls a release-only workflow is detected. Add a regression fixture/test for a caller outside _RUST_CI_WORKFLOWS.
issues.title: Caller audit is not fail-closed over PR-triggered workflows

verdict.summary: The release-only carve-out is reasonable in principle, but its claimed fail-closed inertness proof is incomplete. The regression test checks callers only in a manually maintained subset of workflows, so a future PR-triggered workflow can call an allowlisted reusable release workflow without turning this test red. That would make edits to the called workflow affect a PR check while ci_select still classifies them as orchestration-only.
